gaps.note: commercial break edit hides time taken to consider the offers

stage_a.note: Very strong positive expression, smiling, energetic delivery, 'Let's go baby!'
Pronounced, sustained engagement and excitement throughout the pitch.
Friendly, approachable, uses inclusive gestures and an inviting tone.

venture.description: Performance golf polo shirts with bold, fun patterns aimed at a younger generation of golfers.
venture.note: The two models present do not speak or pitch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Presents Bad Birdie, highlighting the boring nature of traditional golf apparel and offering performance polos with bold, fresh patterns.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: The panel opens the boxes and looks at the sample shirts provided.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes about why anyone would play golf, stating that he hates the sport.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Laughs and acknowledges that he has heard that sentiment from many people.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that golf has a history of being boring, but is becoming more popular with a younger generation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Points out that a person does not actually need to play golf to wear the shirts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees but emphasizes that they are specifically made as performance apparel for use on the golf course.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Compliments the shirts, noting that they are cool looking.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks Mark for the compliment.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: States that he loves golf but notes there is already a lot of similar apparel in the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Counters that existing golf companies have primarily targeted older golfers over the age of forty.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks for the plan to gain market share in the industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shares his background, explaining he invested his own money and achieved seventy-two thousand dollars in sales the first year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Congratulates him on the initial sales achievement.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Adds that in the second year he sold four hundred and twelve thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks to confirm the four hundred and twelve thousand dollar sales figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms the number and states he is currently at seven hundred and sixty thousand, projecting over a million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Expresses being impressed, calling him a hustler.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that sales have been entirely online until the most recent year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks to confirm if the business has been exclusively online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms it was all online, detailing how he releases shirts that sell out rapidly, forcing him to reinvest cash flow.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if customers wait for a specific drop date to buy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees, explaining he does drops every two months, and notes that highly popular designs move into a best sellers category.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mentions that the wildlife design he just highlighted is her favorite.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks how many new designs are dropped per year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States he does about thirty designs per season, alongside limited edition runs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks who is responsible for the design work.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he started doing them himself but has since built a team of about ten designers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks for the manufacturing cost and the retail selling price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Details the selling price and how manufacturing costs have decreased over time, projecting further reductions with overseas production.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks where the shirts are currently being manufactured.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms they are made in Los Angeles and pivots to mention his growing wholesale figures.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Questions the need to expand into retail given the strong online sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Replies that retail presents an opportunity and helps grow the overall brand.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how many units will be produced in each run next year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Estimates that next year's runs will be between one thousand and two thousand per shirt.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Praises the limited drop model, noting it perfectly connects with younger consumers trained by sneaker culture.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees with the assessment.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Challenges the retail strategy, asking if he sees how retail presence kills the urgency of the drop model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concedes the point, acknowledging that he fully sees the difference.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Commends the online momentum and full margin cash flow they currently enjoy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Warns about the dangers of retail apparel deals, stating that many get buried.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies that he only projects keeping retail at twenty-five percent or less of the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Argues that the percentage is irrelevant; the problem is the dynamic with retail buyers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pivots to pricing power, arguing that limited drops allow them to raise prices significantly.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Interrupts to share her thoughts.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Validates the core premise, noting that the shirts effectively stand out amidst the dull competition.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Declares she is out because it is not the right investment for her, despite the good product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks Lori.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Makes an offer based on the strong sales, but explicitly forbids retail expansion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Repeats the terms of the offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reiterates his belief in the drop model, insisting customers should have to beg for the shirts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pushes back on the anti-retail sentiment, arguing that they need to capitalize on their momentum.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Defends his stance, noting he is just riding the current wave.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Jumps in to suggest that if momentum fades, they can always pull back.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Compares the business to another successful online apparel investment and praises the targeted approach.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Makes an offer for twenty-five percent equity, explicitly allowing the founder to decide on retail.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Expresses his fear of the retail market.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Advises him to raise prices but declares he is out because it is not a fit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks Mark.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Explains the harsh realities of retail fees and returns, declaring he is out to avoid putting that pressure on him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Prompts the founder to make a decision between the two standing offers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thinks silently before the edit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Summarizes the offers and pitches his own discipline and experience to win the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Counters Robert's offer, asking if he will drop to twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Refuses the counter, insisting that twenty-five percent is necessary for the partnership.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hesitates, pointing out that twenty-five percent is more than double what he originally asked for.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reminds him that this is the Shark Tank and tough terms are expected.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Acknowledges the environment and asks for a second to think.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Proposes a putting bet to Robert: if Robert makes the putt, he gets twenty-five percent, if he misses, twenty percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Reacts excitedly to the proposed bet.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Enthusiastically agrees to the terms of the putting bet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sets up the putting green for the challenge.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies the rules, establishing that Robert gets only one attempt.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Expresses how much he is enjoying the situation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Boasts about his past golf handicap while preparing for the putt.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells Robert not to miss.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Tells Kevin to be quiet so he can focus.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Playfully tries to distract Robert by chanting for him to miss.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Takes the putt and misses the hole.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Celebrates the miss, securing the deal for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Laughs and calls the outcome fantastic.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Continues bantering and making bets on putting after the deal is closed.

decisions.note: Feels it is not the right investment for her.
Impressed by sales but hates retail apparel deals; forbids retail expansion.
Likes the targeted customer approach and explicitly allows the founder to decide on retail.
Retail scares him and it is not a fit right now.
Does not want to put the pressure of retail fees and returns on the founder.

decisions.terms: Are you willing to go down to 20% on this?
decisions.note: Feels 25% is too much equity to give up.

decisions.terms: If you make a putt, I'll give you 25%. But if you miss the putt, it's 20%.
decisions.note: Proposes a golf bet to settle the equity difference.
Agrees to the terms of the putting bet for either 20% or 25%.
Accepts the 20% deal after Robert misses the putt.

record.notes: The deal is concluded through a putting bet between the founder and investor.
